title: Copilot Studio: agent node runs an AI agent as a workflow step
summary: The briefing's roadmap facts, controls and consumption-based licensing are supported. Both API calls are documented, including the allocation request body; the stated gaps remain appropriately limited to agent-node-specific documentation.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is Launched.
claims.quote: "status": "Launched"

claims.claim: The roadmap target date is September CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "September CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap preview date is April CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "April CY2026"

claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; summary; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Workflow and agent usage use consumption-based billing measured in Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Usage is billed based on consumption and measured in Copilot Credits. Creating and using agents, workflows, and apps consumes credits based on usage and rate of consumption.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The documented Microsoft 365 Copilot coverage for workflows is when run inside a standard harness agent by a licensed user, with billing in all other cases.
claims.quote: | Workflows | Yes, when run inside a standard harness agent by a licensed user | Billed in all other cases. |

claims.claim: The cost rating is variable because the feature consumes metered Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: The harness used to build this agent uses usage-based billing. Using, building, testing, and evaluating agents might consume Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: Credit allocation is under Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Manage Copilot Credits.
claims.quote:
In the navigation pane, select **Licensing**.
3. Under **Products**, select **Copilot Studio**.
4. Select **Manage Copilot Credits**.

claims.claim: PUT https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=2024-10-01 writes the environment allocation using the documented MCSMessages and TenantPool request body.
claims.quote:
Invoke-RestMethod -Method Put `
    -Uri "$apiBaseUrl/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=$apiVersion" `
    -Headers $headers -ContentType "application/json" -Body $allocationBody

claims.claim: Workflow capacity consumption can be reviewed in Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Copilot Studio.
claims.quote: In the [Power Platform admin center](https://admin.powerplatform.microsoft.com/) > **Licensing** > **Copilot Studio**, review the **Agent flow actions** used by each workflow.

claims.claim: The documented environment resource consumption call is GET /licensing/entitlements/MCSMessages/environments/<environment ID>/resources with fromDate, toDate and api-version=2024-10-01.
claims.quote: GET https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/entitlements/{entitlementId}/environments/{environmentId}/resources?fromDate={fromDate}&toDate={toDate}&api-version=2024-10-01

claims.claim: The maker path is Workflows > workflow > Build > Add panel > Agent > Request human assistance when unsure.
claims.quote:
Existing workflow: Open the workflow and go to the **Build** tab.
2. Select the **Agent** icon on the Add panel.

Turn on **Request human assistance when unsure** to let the agent escalate when it isn't confident enough to act on its own.

claims.claim: No API for the node's Request human assistance when unsure setting is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Request human assistance when unsure" API administrator policy. Read agent-node-workflow and search results: the setting is described in the maker UI; no configuration API was found.

claims.where: controls[3]; summary; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: No tenant switch dedicated to disabling the agent node, or dedicated node switches for its Work IQ and knowledge settings, is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "agent node" "disable"; "agent node" "Work IQ" "policy". Read agent-node-workflow, manage-usage-github-copilot-harness, admin-data-loss-prevention, advanced-connector-policies and policy-governance-mcp: no dedicated node switch found.

claims.claim: Capacity management requires Power Platform Administrator, Global Administrator, or an equivalent role that can manage licensing and capacity.
claims.quote: To manage Copilot Studio capacity, you need the Power Platform Administrator or Global Administrator role, or an equivalent role that can manage licensing and capacity.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Cost and licensing; Governance controls
claims.claim: Environment capacity controls apply across Copilot Studio rather than exclusively to workflows containing agent nodes.
claims.quote: The capacity and consumption controls in the Power Platform admin center apply across Copilot Studio. They aren't exclusive to the Microsoft Copilot harness.

claims.claim: Changing shared capacity can affect other agents, workflows and features in the same environment.
claims.quote: Changes to shared capacity can affect other Copilot Studio agents, workflows, and features in the same environment.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Allocating credits and clearing Draw from the available capacity in my tenant caps prepaid consumption at the environment allocation.
claims.quote: To contain prepaid consumption, allocate a defined amount of Copilot Credits to the environment and turn off **Draw from the available capacity in my tenant**.

claims.claim: Disabling tenant-pool draw does not stop consumption through a linked pay-as-you-go billing plan.
claims.quote: If the environment is linked to a pay-as-you-go billing plan, usage can continue through the linked Azure subscription.

claims.claim: Azure budgets and alerts notify rather than stopping Copilot Studio usage.
claims.quote: Azure budgets and alerts send notifications but don't stop Copilot Studio consumption.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: An agent node hands a workflow step to an AI agent that can reason before returning a result.
claims.quote: The agent node lets a flow hand a step over to an AI agent that can reason, call tools, and pull from knowledge sources before returning a result.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The agent can call attached tools to take actions.
claims.quote: Tools give the agent the ability to *do* actions such as send a message, query a record, run a search, or call an API.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The agent can ground responses in attached knowledge.
claims.quote: When you ask the agent a question, it can ground its answer in the sources you attach instead of relying only on what the model already knows.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The response is available as dynamic content to subsequent workflow steps.
claims.quote: The agent response then becomes available as dynamic content that you can use in any subsequent step.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: The node documentation does not specify the credential identity used for attached connector actions or SharePoint knowledge.
claims.quote: Searched: "agent node" "identity" "SharePoint". Read the full agent-node-workflow page, including Tools and Knowledge; it names the Work IQ running user and assistance connection owner but does not state connector-action or SharePoint-knowledge execution identity.

claims.claim: The node Learn page does not identify which part of the feature remains in preview.
claims.quote: Searched: "agent node" "preview". Read agent-node-workflow in full; no delineation of Preview versus General Availability is given for its capabilities.

claims.claim: The node page names no licence among prerequisites for adding the node.
claims.quote: Searched: licence, license and prerequisites in the full agent-node-workflow page. It provides Add an agent node instructions and a usage-based billing note but no named licence prerequisite.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: The checked documentation does not explicitly confirm that Work IQ MCP policy governs the inline agent node's Work IQ option.
claims.quote: Searched: "agent node" "Work IQ" "policy". Read agent-node-workflow, policy-governance-mcp and the add-work-iq search excerpt; the node toggle is not explicitly mapped to Work IQ MCP tenant policy.

claims.claim: The checked Learn documentation does not explicitly establish that individual-agent monthly limits cap an agent node inside a workflow.
claims.quote: Searched: "agent node" "credits" "rate" workflow monthly limit. Read manage-usage-github-copilot-harness, agent-node-workflow and capacity search excerpts; individual-agent limits are documented, but their application to a workflow agent node is not stated.

claims.claim: No central enforcement setting for Request human assistance when unsure is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Request human assistance when unsure" API administrator policy. Read agent-node-workflow and returned excerpts: the per-node maker toggle is documented, with no central enforcement setting found.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: Data policies govern Power Platform connector tools in Copilot Studio agents.
claims.quote: To prevent agent makers from [using Power Platform connectors as tools](advanced-connectors) in Copilot Studio agents, configure a data policy with the connectors you want to block.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Blocking Power Platform connectors also blocks tools in connected MCP servers that rely on those connectors.
claims.quote: Blocking Power Platform connectors also blocks access to tools in connected MCP servers, which rely on Power Platform connectors for connectivity.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Advanced Connector Policies govern certified connectors through the hosting environment's policy.
claims.quote: At runtime, when a connector operation is invoked, it queries the effective policy for the current hosting environment.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Advanced Connector Policies support MCP server blocking.
claims.quote: Within advanced connector policies, administrators can see MCP servers listed alongside other connector types and can choose to block an entire MCP server.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Custom and HTTP connectors still require classic data policies rather than ACP.
claims.quote: Custom connectors and HTTP connectors aren't yet supported. They're planned as a separate rule type in the future. For governing custom connectors and HTTP connectors today, continue using classic [data policies](prevent-data-loss).

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: ACP design-time enforcement is rolling out to Copilot Studio, and enforcement is runtime-only until design-time support is available.
claims.quote:
**Copilot Studio** — following Power Automate

Until design-time support is available in a given maker portal, ACP operates as a runtime-only enforcement for that workload.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Items blocked by a data policy or ACP appear disabled in the Microsoft Copilot harness agent's tool, model and skill pickers.
claims.quote: When a data policy or Advanced Connector Policy blocks a tool, connector, AI model, or skill, that item appears disabled wherever you'd normally select it, such as the tools list, model list, or skills list.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Work IQ MCP has a tenant-level policy control.
claims.quote: In the initial release, Work IQ MCP provides tenant-level policy control. In the Microsoft 365 admin center, tenant administrators can turn Work IQ MCP policy on or off for the tenant.
